workingState: uncommitted implementation patch based on baseRevision

slices.acceptanceStatement: An authorized tenant caller can submit critical-transfer operational context, report attempt-aware progress through the real agent HTTP and Raft path, and read a tenant-isolated transfer progress resource that distinguishes lifecycle state from operational condition and exposes source-size, freshness, ownership, deadline, active-attempt, and retry context.
slices.failureBoundary: Before implementation, the real transfer-submission boundary must reject the unsupported operational context; after implementation, the same end-to-end path must return committed context and a late REQUIRED_COMPLETION_MISSED condition without bypassing HTTP, tenant authorization, attempt fencing, or Raft.

red.patchIdentity: base revision plus failing test only
red.expectedFailure: POST /api/v1/transfers returned 400 instead of 201 because the operational context was not accepted or persisted.
red.outcome: failed as expected before production implementation

green.patchIdentity: working implementation patch based on baseRevision

refactorSummary: Kept operational context in the existing transfer metadata model and added a typed snapshot projection so Raft persistence and legacy snapshot construction remain compatible.
Derived the progress read model from authoritative transfer, assignment, and attempt state instead of creating a second mutable source of truth.
Registered the resource in the existing HTTP, discovery, authorization, and OpenAPI conventions.
slices.sensitiveEvidenceStatement: Evidence contains build output and synthetic tenant, service, transfer, agent, and runbook identifiers only; it contains no credentials, keys, request bodies, or production payloads.

slices.acceptanceStatement: A submitted transfer with no advancing byte report exposes telemetry as UNKNOWN, does not invent a last-progress time or telemetry age, and does not represent the absence of telemetry as fresh zero-byte progress.
slices.failureBoundary: The real tenant-checked progress endpoint must distinguish transfer creation and lifecycle updates from an actual increase in transferred bytes.

red.patchIdentity: preceding Phase 3 patch plus failing test only
red.expectedFailure: The endpoint returned FRESH because transfer last-update time was incorrectly treated as last-progress time.
red.outcome: failed as expected before production implementation

refactorSummary: Added a backward-compatible lastProgressAt snapshot field distinct from generic lifecycle lastUpdateTime.
Only an increase in authoritative transferred bytes advances lastProgressAt; status-only and repeated same-byte reports do not hide a stall.

slices.acceptanceStatement: Controller-governed freshness and stall windows drive the tenant-checked progress condition and the effective windows and policy source are disclosed to an operator caller.
slices.failureBoundary: A progress observation ten seconds old is STALE and DEGRADED under a configured five-second freshness window but is not STALLED before the configured fifteen-second stall window.

red.patchIdentity: preceding Phase 3 patch plus failing test only
red.expectedFailure: The endpoint returned FRESH because it used a fixed sixty-second implementation constant and did not disclose effective policy.
red.outcome: failed as expected before production implementation

refactorSummary: Moved freshness and stall windows into validated controller configuration while retaining established defaults.
Injected immutable durations into the handler at route construction and exposed their effective values and source in the progress contract.

slices.acceptanceStatement: A tenant caller can submit a transfer and retrieve its first ordered TRANSFER_SUBMITTED event with deterministic identity, sequence, time, tenant, business-service, and state context.

red.expectedFailure: The event resource returned 404 before the route and ledger existed.

refactorSummary: Used command timestamps and per-transfer sequence values so Raft replicas derive identical records.
Included the ledger in snapshots and exposed it only after tenant verification.

slices.acceptanceStatement: A tenant caller can retrieve a canonically named TRANSFER_ASSIGNED event, correlated to the authoritative attempt and agent, immediately after TRANSFER_SUBMITTED, and the ordered ledger remains intact across controller snapshot reset and restore.

red.expectedFailure: Snapshot restore rejected an unintended Jackson empty property exposed by the operational-context helper.
After the restart-boundary defect was corrected, the restored ledger contained only TRANSFER_SUBMITTED and lacked the assignment event.
The event used ATTEMPT_OFFERED rather than the established canonical TRANSFER_ASSIGNED vocabulary.

refactorSummary: Excluded the internal isEmpty helper from the persisted JSON contract without changing operational-context data.
Appended assignment events in the same replicated command that creates the assignment and first fenced attempt.
Retained attempt-level detail while using the canonical transfer-level event vocabulary already defined by the architecture specification.

slices.acceptanceStatement: A critical financial-services transfer exposes an ordered canonical timeline from submission through assignment, acceptance, start, and progress, with attempt, agent, byte, total-size, and report-sequence correlation.

red.expectedFailure: The timeline contained two events instead of the required five because acceptance, start, and progress events were absent.

refactorSummary: Generated lifecycle events inside the existing atomic replicated lifecycle command after all transition validations pass.
Preserved exact-retry idempotency because duplicate reports return before event append.
Extended the event schema with optional byte, total-size, and report-sequence evidence required to explain operational progress.

slices.acceptanceStatement: An active transfer with no byte advancement beyond the configured stall window is reported as STALLED and discloses the stable condition onset and elapsed stall duration needed for operator triage.

red.expectedFailure: The response classified the active transfer as STALLED but omitted conditionSince and stallDurationSeconds.

refactorSummary: Derived condition onset from the authoritative last-progress time plus the effective controller stall window.
Kept condition evaluation read-only; the progress query does not mutate state or manufacture durable events.
Added optional timing fields to the OpenAPI progress schema without weakening missing-telemetry semantics.
